coverage: Traced all five copper segments in inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb by coordinate arithmetic against pad positions: /IN segment (100,100)-(104.0875,100) joins J1 pad1 to R1 pad1; /OUT segment (105.9125,100)-(109.05,100) joins R1 pad2 to C1 pad1; /OUT branch (100,102.54)-(107.5,102.54)-(107.5,100) joins J1 pad2 to a point lying exactly on the R1-C1 /OUT segment; GND segment (110.95,100)-(113,100) joins C1 pad2 to the GND via.

Cross-checked every board pad net assignment against the schematic netlist (work/netlist/design.xml, work/netlist/connectivity.json): /IN={J1.1,R1.1}, /OUT={C1.1,J1.2,R1.2}, GND={C1.2,J1.3}; board and schematic agree, consistent with the zero-parity DRC result.

Independently verified the geometry criterion from the native board file: all five segments carry (width 0.25), satisfying the declared 0.20 mm minimum; zone min_thickness is also 0.25 mm; this matches work/geometry/geometry.json.

Read the saved B.Cu GND zone filled_polygon vertex list: it is a single connected polygon spanning (96.5,96.5)-(115.5,107.5), covering the via location (113,100) with no cutout, with ~1.35 mm anti-pad cutouts around J1 pads 1 and 2 (/IN, /OUT) and a thermal-relief (spoked) connection pattern around J1 pad 3 (GND), so the C1.2 -> via -> B.Cu zone -> J1.3 return path is continuous as saved.

Checked placement and outline: board is 20 x 12 mm (Edge.Cuts 96-116 x, 96-108 y); all footprint courtyards (J1 x 98.23-101.77 / y 98.23-106.85; R1 x 103.32-106.68; C1 x 108.3-111.7) are inside the outline and do not overlap; the via at (113,100) is ~3 mm from the nearest edge; the /OUT branch at y=102.54 clears the R1/C1 pad rows at y=100+/-0.7.

Recomputed the analytic RC response for R=10k, C=100n (tau=1 ms): 1-e^-1=0.632121 V at 1 ms and 1-e^-5=0.993262 V at 5 ms, matching ngspice measurements 0.6321201 and 0.9932621 in work/rc-step/ngspice.log, and within the declared 0.62-0.65 V window at 1 ms.

Checked the simulation deck (work/rc-step/deck.cir) element-by-element against the exported netlist: C1 OUT-0 100n and R1 IN-OUT 10k match design.xml nets with GND mapped to node 0; the PWL(0 0 1n 1) stimulus is an acceptable approximation of the ideal step for a 1 ms time constant.

Reviewed schematic wiring and labels in inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch: local labels IN/OUT and the GND power symbols produce the three expected nets, GND carries a PWR_FLAG, and ERC reported zero violations across one sheet.

findings.condition: There is no front-copper connection between C1 pad 2 (GND) and J1 pad 3 (GND); the only GND path is the 2.05 mm F.Cu segment to one via (0.6 mm pad / 0.3 mm drill) into the B.Cu zone, which reaches J1.3 only through thermal-relief spokes.

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb (via uuid b71a70d7-bbc1-43d1-ae55-5e4d992412a4 at 113,100; zone uuid 38a83012-bcf9-4bb9-b9f4-50d49cd91d90 on B.Cu)
findings.mechanism: If the zone fill is ever regenerated differently (the packet itself notes a refill pass was forbidden), or the single via is compromised (drill breakout, barrel crack, assembly rework), the entire GND net opens and the filter output floats; there is no redundant path.
findings.reasoning: I verified the saved fill is a single connected polygon that covers the via and connects J1.3 via spokes, so connectivity holds as saved and DRC's zero unconnected items is corroborated. This is a robustness concern, not a saved-state defect: for a disposable fixture it is acceptable, but it is the one single-point dependency in the board's electrical integrity and worth recording.
findings.title: GND return depends entirely on the saved zone fill and a single 0.3 mm-drill via

findings.condition: The vertical /OUT segment from J1 pad 2 ends at (107.5,100), which is not a pad or a segment endpoint but a point on the interior of the (105.9125,100)-(109.05,100) /OUT segment.
findings.mechanism: KiCad's geometric connectivity accepts a track end landing on another track's body (DRC reports 0 unconnected items, and the point lies exactly on the 0.25 mm-wide run, so copper overlap is real). However, a T-junction without a shared node is fragile under future edits: dragging or re-routing the horizontal segment can silently open the J1.2 connection without changing any endpoint coordinates.
findings.reasoning: As saved, the junction is electrically sound; I confirmed (107.5,100) lies on the horizontal /OUT segment at identical y with full width overlap. Flagged informationally because the connectivity is positional rather than topological, which is a known maintenance hazard.
findings.title: /OUT branch terminates mid-segment rather than at a shared endpoint or pad

findings.condition: The geometry probe console contains three 'assert "m_choices.GetCount() > 0" failed in PROPERTY_ENUM()' messages from kicad/include/properties/property.h(607), and execution.json records a non-empty stderr hash, yet the check exited 0 and was recorded as pass.
findings.mechanism: Debug assertions firing inside the pcbnew Python bindings indicate the tool ran in a partially inconsistent state; a successful exit is not proof the extraction was complete, so the pass verdict rests on tool output that showed internal errors.
findings.reasoning: I independently re-derived the geometry result from the native board file: exactly five segments, all width 0.25 mm, matching geometry.json's counts, widths, pad list, and via. The assertions therefore did not corrupt this run's data, but the tool-health signal should be known to the operator since future runs on larger boards might not be so easily hand-verified.
findings.title: Geometry probe emitted repeated pcbnew assertion failures

findings.condition: The rc-step criterion declares two measurements but only vout_1ms has min/max bounds; vout_5ms (measured 0.9932621 V) has min and max of null, so it cannot fail.

evidence.locator: requirement 1 (only the 1 ms window is specified)

findings.mechanism: An unbounded measurement adds no verification power: a gross error visible only in the settled value (for example a leakage path or wrong divider that still happens to pass the 1 ms window) would be recorded but never flagged. The 1 ms window alone does constrain R*C tightly (0.62-0.65 V maps to roughly tau = 0.93-1.05 ms), so coverage of the declared requirement 1 is real, but the settled-value check is decorative.
findings.reasoning: This matches the declared requirement, which only bounds the 1 ms point, so it is not a defect; I recorded it because the review brief asks for independent challenge of verification coverage and stimuli. I confirmed the measured 5 ms value equals the analytic 1-e^-5 for the intended RC, so the unloaded response is in fact correct.
findings.title: vout_5ms measurement carries no acceptance limits

limitations: I had no tools; all conclusions come from reading the native files and check records. Zone fill connectivity was assessed by manually interpreting the saved filled_polygon vertices, not by a refill or a connectivity engine; a subtle break in the spoke geometry at J1.3 cannot be fully excluded from vertex inspection alone.
work/rc-step/result.raw is binary and was not readable; transient values were taken from the .meas lines in work/rc-step/ngspice.log and corroborated analytically.

No stackup, copper weight, or current requirement is declared, so ampacity and thermal adequacy of the 0.25 mm tracks and the single 0.3 mm-drill GND via were not and cannot be assessed; the 0.20 mm rule is geometric only, per the declared requirements.

DRC clearance results were accepted from the tool record; I spot-checked only the most likely conflicts (the /OUT branch versus the R1/C1 pad rows and the zone anti-pads) rather than exhaustively recomputing all clearances.
Tolerance, temperature, external loading, soldermask/paste correctness, and silkscreen legibility were not evaluated, consistent with the packet's declared scope limits.
